text:
Marta G.: hey team — quick question. planning to move my base from Dublin -> SF on Apr 15, but i'll be working from EU ~3 days/week for the first 12 weeks. can i keep EU benefits and still get the wfh stipend? also worried about tax nexus / payroll cutover. any do's/don'ts? :thinking_face:

Sam (People Ops): hey @Marta G. :wave: good Q. Quick summary: homebase determines payroll + benefits by default. split-location arrangements are possible but need approvals (people-ops + payroll + tax). we'll need a Homebase Change + Hybrid Exception. can you share proposed dates?

Marta G.: dates are Apr 15 -> Jul 7 (12 weeks). i'll be in SF mon/tue, Dublin wed-fri for that window. hoping stipend starts from Apr 15 and is prorated.

Sam (People Ops): got it. policy notes:
- WFH stipend is paid to the active homebase payroll country. when homebase changes, stipend and benefits move with payroll.
- For temporary hybrid splits like yours, we typically: 1) keep original homebase for benefits if <=90 days abroad and tax team confirms no nexus, or 2) flip homebase if >90 days or if local regs require it. your 12-week window is borderline, so we need tax ops sign-off.
- Next steps: please fill the Homebase Change form + Hybrid Exception form: https://intra.redwood/caseforms/homebase (pick "temporary split")

Nina (Payroll): heads-up from payroll side:
- Payroll cutover can take 6–8 weeks from submission (registrations, local tax paperwork).
- If we keep Dublin as payroll but you spend >60 days in US in a calendar year we may need to withhold US taxes or register in the US. need to check SSN/ITIN and state withholding.
- Action items for Marta: attach copy of passport, US SSN (if available), and exact travel schedule to the form.

Jorge (Benefits): quick on benefits:
- Our EU medical plan doesn't cover routine care in the US. if you keep Dublin homebase and travel to SF, you may need to enroll in local travel/expat coverage or rely on out-of-network reimbursement.
- Short-term option: we can enroll you in the Global Medical Rider for up to 90 days, but after that you'll need a local plan.
- Please don't cancel Dublin plan yet until Payroll confirms homebase status.

Raj (Finance): from expense & stipend POV:
- Stipend proration: we do monthly pro-rata from change date. formula we use: `prorated_stipend = monthly_stipend * days_in_month_on_new_policy / days_in_month` (we can do a manual calc for Apr).
- Relocation/shipping: if you request company shipping for two-way move (equipment), file the Relocation request. approvals required.
- If tax nexus triggered for the company in the US state where you'll be located, that may change withholding and employer-side filings. we'll coordinate if Tax Ops flags risk.

Claire (Legal): immigration note: make sure you have right-to-work for US (visa/SSN). if you're a dual national, drop that on the form. if not, speak to Legal before booking travel — can't start payroll cutover before verifying status.

Payroll Bot: New case created: HB-4521 — "Marta G. temporary Dublin->SF hybrid". Assigned: Sam (People Ops), Nina (Payroll), TaxOps.

Marta G.: thanks all — super helpful. one quick ask: if tax ops says no nexus, can i still get SF-based per-diem for office co-working days?

Sam (People Ops): yes, coworking per-diems are typically location-based and can be approved even if homebase stays in Dublin. include requested per-diem days in the form and we can route for manager + finance approval. :white_check_mark:

Marta G.: perfect. i'll submit the forms today and attach passport + travel schedule. thanks everyone! :pray:
